category_title: Children with ASD requiring high structure and emotional regulation support
minimal_context: The class is transitioning to group discussion time, with the children expected to congregate around the teacher on the carpet.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our group discussion. Please come congregate on the carpet with the other children.

STUDENT: (Opts to sit at his desk) I am staying at my desk.

TUTOR: We need everyone together for the discussion. Please find a spot on the carpet.

STUDENT: No, I dislike the disorder and clutter of sitting with the other children down there.

TUTOR: You need to join us on the carpet right now so we can start.

STUDENT: (Becomes angry) I said no! I am not sitting in that clutter!

options.A: Employ visual or gestural prompts to direct the student to the carpet.
options.B: Provide a detailed instruction of each specific element in the group discussion.
options.C: Reinforce the desired behavior with a high five or a verbal compliment.
options.D: Seat the children in a circle while the tutor remains outside the circle.
